body: The Trincomalee War Cemetery is a solemn and beautifully maintained memorial located on the Trincomalee-Nilaveli Road. It serves as the final resting place for British Empire soldiers who lost their lives during World War II.The cemetery is known for its serene atmosphere, featuring perfectly manicured lawns and rows of white headstones. It primarily honors those from the Royal Navy and Royal Air Force who defended the strategic port. It is a significant historical site for travelers seeking a moment of reflection.
title: Trincomalee War Cemetery

body: A real credit to the Commonwealth war graves commission whose staff maintain this place beautifully. Contains French and Italian graves as well as Commonwealth service people. Was particularly struck by one joint headstone for three young aviators killed on landing who are interred together. A place for quiet reflection for those mostly young people who gave their lives for our freedom
title: We will remember them

body: Having read about the Japanese raid on Trincomolee and Colombo during WW2 and the loss of over 600 men, 20 ships and one of our aircraft carriers, I really wanted to come and pay my respects at the War Grave Memorial and really enjoyed the experience. body: This is a really peaceful place to disappear to and escape the hussle and bussle of Trincomalee roads. Very tranquil setting, which encourages quiet reflection. I went twice. body: The War Cemetery is just north of Trincomalee, it’s not very big but you can’t really miss it, it’s on the right heading north.There are apparently 303 WW2 graves and other Merchant and non war graves.There are flowers, cacti, and other type of plants in between and around the graves and they really look well with differing colours, the site is really very well looked after. I spoke with a caretaker of the site he told me a lot of the graves where men from an aircraft carrier that was sunk by Japanese forces out of Batticaloa.This is an excerpt from amazinglanka.com“The Trincomalee cemetery was originally the Combined Services Cemetery, but was taken over by the Admiralty from the military authorities in April 1948 for use as a permanent naval cemetery. On the withdrawal of United Kingdom Forces from Ceylon it became the property of the Ceylon Government is today maintained by the Ministry of Defense on behalf of the Commonwealth War Graves Commission.The cemetery records 303 world war II causalities. Save for a few post-war and non-war graves it is purely a war cemetery, and service war graves were transferred to it from Trincomalee (St. Mary) Churchyard; Trincomalee (St. Stephen’s) Cemetery, Kottadi Cemetery, Jaffna; and Vavuiyna Combined Cemetery. A special memorial commemorates a naval man buried in Trincomalee (St. Stephen’s) Cemetery whose grave could not be found.The non-war graves are those of men of the Merchant Navy whose death was not due to war service, and of civilians, of whom some were employees of the Admiralty; while the post-war graves were dependents of servicemen, civilian employees of the Admiralty and dependents of such employees.”It’s worth a visit just to remember.
title: Trincomalee War Cemetery

body: There is something very sobering about wandering around a War Cemetery and reading the headstones. All those lost young men, some as young and 18, gone before their lives had started.As a mother of sons, I found the whole experience very moving and a reminder of why we must avoid future wars and why we must learn from our past.The cemetery is set in beautiful garden like grounds and is very well kept. It is a place where these mostly British soldiers and sailors can rest in peace and not be forgotten. It is one of the six Commonwealth war cemeteries in Sri Lanka, and is maintained by Sri Lankan Ministry of Defense on behalf of the Commonwealth War Graves Commission.
title: Poignant and sobering

body: The Commonwealth War Cemetery is in Uppuveli a fewkilometres north of Trincomalee. Expect to pay 400 rupeesfor a tuk-tuk from the south/centre of Trincomalee.Thecemetery is beautifully maintained and holds the gravesof 362 military personnel. A visit is a moving and sombre experience. For me the most moving moment was findingthe grave of a young man who died on the day I was born.There are many nationalities buried together here includingBritish, Indians, Italians, Australians, Canadians, Dutch and Burmese. Those buried here include those killed in the Japanese air raid on Trincomalee in April 1942. A visit isstrongly recommended.
title: A moving and sombre experience.

body: This is a well kept war cemetery on the Nilaveli road within easy walking distance of the Trinco Blu hotel. There is a visitor’s book that the caretaker holds and who also keeps the site so beautifully. We were very pleasantly surprised to see how many visitors had already signed the book in 2017. Most of those buried here were British Royal or Merchant Navy servicemen but there were other nationalities and faiths and, as it should be, there was no discrimination on the location a grave by nationality, faith or rank. The terrible tragedy of war is brought home by the age of many of those buried here, most were in their late teens and early twenties. Some headstones had inscriptions from parents who had lost their only son - truly heartrending to read.

Lots were British sailors, soldiers, and nurses but there is also a sprinkling of other Nationals who assisted in various ways and gave the ultimate sacrifice. body: A well maintained cemetery. We walked around the tombstones and were heartbroken to see the lives that were lost as a result of the war. A good place to spend some time and discuss the futility of war.
title: Interesting, but nothing much to do here

body: Our driver drew our attention to this cemetery in passing on our way to Nilaveli and I prevailed on him to return the following day as this was the 11th Nov. That this was an auspicious date was lost on him at first.This cemetery is beautifully kept and anyone who has a relative here should know that the guys are being well cared for. I met the man in charge of the upkeep and thanked him for his obvious devotion to the job. There are servicemen here from all over the commonwealth - Canada, Africa and NZ are represented and almost everywhere in between including several Dutch sailors.Next door is a school and as you walk around the graves you can hear the children laughing and playing without a care in the world which is just as it should be.
title: The 11th.

body: Stopped had a little look round was very well kept men there tiding Nice to see looked after on a nice place to lay to rest and in peace
title: War cemetery

body: Most of the tombstones show how young the men were who perished in the war...what a waste of life. The Cemetry is well maintained though
title: Remembering the sacrifice made

body: First came across the cemetery in 2002, when it stood out all exposed on the Nilaveli - Trincomalee road. This time, although we were staying just round the corner at Cinnamon Trinco blu we set off to visit again we actually drove past three times before finding it as shrubbery and trees have grown around it, concealing it from either side. However the experience is just as moving emotionally and having visited many of the Commonwealth war graves in France, the graveyard is just as well maintained by the current caretaker who took over from his father. A must visit location if in the Trincomalee area
title: Moving experience

body: We just stumbled over this while out exploring. I try to visit Commonwealth War Cemeteries wherever I go so thus was a fortunate find.Like most Commonwealth Cemeteries this is well maintained and cared for.The caretaker is a lovely man who will help you find particular graves or nationalities.It is a fitting resting place for our fallen.Lest We Forget.
title: A peaceful place to sit and contemplate.

body: This is very close to the Cinnamon Blu hotel and its good to stop over and visit this cemetery. there is a caretaker and he will help you out with any questions you would have about the deceased. The garden had lots and lots of butterflies. (that time of the year, I guess) Please remember to sign on the guest book with your thoughts.
title: A beautiful place

body: I cried... I never cry in graveyards...Learn about Trincomalee before you come here. Get an understanding then come see it for yourself.It's rather small but enough to hit you in the face...the caretaker is unreal. His knowledge is above the rest and we have him 500R for the tour and wasn't disappointed at all...
title: The history!

body: Really nice to see now well kept this cemetery is. Definitely worth a visit if you are interested in colonial and military history.
title: Beautifully kept

body: We stopped and got down the tuk tuk when we were on the way to the city.Glad we stopped and spent few minutes reading the tombstone inscriptions.It was touching and sad to see the age and the message from loved ones. Well maintained place.
title: Touching!

body: Well organized & well maintained. The person who incharged is very friendly & informative. Several times I've been there with my clients. Also there are another 3 world war cemeteries around the island. One in kandy & two in colombo. Kandy cemetery is very beautiful. Worth watching.
title: Very well maintained.

body: So sad to see so many long men give their lifes but nice to see it so well looked after. We were nicely greeted and invited to sign the visitors book.
title: Beautifully kept

body: We paid our second visit to the cemetery and were welcomed by the curator whose knowledge of the numbers and nationalities of the occupants is impressive. He pointed out the tree planted by Princess Anne on her visit 20 years ago, and was kind enough to show me some photographs of that occasion, when his father was curator (for 27 years in all). The last time we visited the ground was dry and the grass parched; this time it was lush and green and beautifully tended. A credit to the curator.
title: Beautifully kept reminder of the sacrifice of others

body: Five minutes walk from Trinco Blu and well worth a visit. The caretaker showed us around - his father was the caretaker before him - and it's beautifully cared for and rather humbling.
title: Moving experience

body: The cemetery is about 5-10 minutes walk from the turnoff for both the Trinco Blu and the Amaranthe hotels. It's from World War 2 and commemorates the Christian, Buddhist, Hindu and Muslim soldiers who died in the war. If you are looking for a specific headstone then you could either look it up beforehand on the Commonwealth War Graves Commmission website or talk to the wonderful caretaker there, Mr Vasantha Raja, who has known the place all his life and followed his fathers footsteps into the role. He will show you around the small site and point out some key plots. He and colleagues also maintain a fantastic selection of plants around the headstones. Don't miss it.
title: Peaceful, beautiful cemetery , don't miss it.

body: Located a few minutes outside Trincomalee, and a couple of minutes from Cinnamon Blu, the cemetery is beautifully maintained. It is remarkably tranquil given its proximity to the road, giving a sense of reflection and remembrance.The grounds are relatively small, but are perfectly maintained by the son of the original groundsman. He is proud of his work, including.It is free to visit, however we felt a donation was the right thing to do.
title: Beautifully maintained as a tribute

body: I know bad pun, but this place is a gem if you like war history and the caretaker is a really nice chap who tells you about the graves. It's really well kept, most graves are British but some Sri Lankans, New Zealanders, British,I was keen to see the graves of the British fallen, very moving.
title: Grave mistake to miss it 😩

body: The age of those buried here seems to average around twenty. The whole place is well maintained, orderly and as with all official war graves there is a guide book present to help you find out more. There are Christian, Hindu, Jewish and Muslim graves. Indian labourers lie alongside Royal Marine Commandos. War knows no religion or caste. All are equal in death. We didn't find sailors from the ship we were looking for (HMS Cornwall sunk in these parts, my wife's Grandfather was on board and recovered in Tricomolee we wondered if he had ship mates here we should pay respects to on his behalf) but we found hundreds of stories that deserve to be told. We found a painful and quiet place that doesn't glorify war but shows the reality of it.
title: Very moving

body: A beautifully kept cemetery to have a look around. The caretaker was there and showed us some information and letters etc relating to the cemetery. We enjoyed meeting him and couldn't help but be impressed by his pride in looking after this lovely place of remembrance. Well worth stopping to visit.
title: A loevley place to stop and visit

body: Before going we didn't expect a lot, but it was overwhelming. Very well kept, very decent, very respectfully cemetery for those who left their lives in the Second World War in Sri Lanka, Ceylon at those times. I wish a cemetery like this for al the people who died during the Sri Lankan civil war, especially for them, 40.000 refugees, who died in May 2010 during the final bombings on the small beach-strip of Mulaitivu, which was actually a safe non-fire zone.
title: Very well kept cemetery!

body: Well maintained and taken care of. It appeared closed when we went there, but then we opened the gate and approached what looked like the caretaker's house and asked his permission. he then got his son to open the main gate and let us in. You can park on the main road and go in. It is sad that not a lot people visit this beautiful place.
title: Hauntingly Beautiful!

body: We stopped by here and were moved by the small tour we were taken on the caretaker. Well worth the visit.
title: Unique and moving small cemetary

body: We visited in the afternoon, after a short walk from our hotel. When we entered through the gates we were greeted by the caretaker, who showed us around and sat down with us and told us about the cementery and the soldiers whose remains are buried in the graves. It was very moving to read the comments left by the families on the tomb stones. The cementery is well taken care of and definitely worth a visit.
title: Very moving

body: This is the first cemetery where I saw tombstones of Hindus,Muslims ,Sikhs and Christians all in one place. They were all soldiers who lost,mostly their young lives, in the second world war.The Cemetery is well maintained with loving care by planting flowers on each tombstone and keeping it neat and clean.
title: A unique resting place for soldiers of different nationalities and religions.

body: Located off the main road between Trincomalee and Nilaveli this war cemetery is a beautifully maintained tribute to those foreign troops who fell in Sri Lanka during World War Two. Given the harsh climatic conditions of this area it is nothing short of amazing how the landscaping is kept in the manicured state it is in. Highly recommended.
title: A beautiful tribute to those who fell in World War Two

body: Do visit if you are in the area - it is immaculate & moving. How to find it: From the main A6 road, just south of the town of Trincomalee, turn left onto the North East Coast Road, also known as the Nilaveli Road. The cemetery is approximately 6 kilometres along this road on the right (eastern) side.
title: Sad to read on the gravestones how young so many were. A beautifully kept cemetery

body: Usually war cemeteries can be a bit grim, but here all the plants between the graves make it a peaceful place.We almost thought the stones were new but the caretaker told us they are cleaned every 2-3 month.All these mostly very young man...
title: Beautiful cemetery

body: I always visit war cemetery's when I travel - out of respect and because maybe families cant visit their lost ones at these locations. This is perhaps one of the best presented and cared for cemetery's I've seen. The grounds men take great care and are so enthusiastic to speak to you about the grave and tell you the history.
title: Please visit, a really well presented cemetery

body: I intednd to dive the wreck HMS Hermes. Feli the Tec dive instructor mentioned that three bodies of soldiers of the wreck hermes are buried here. I found them.I entered my name in the visitors book.
title: Very well maintained.

body: We stopped to pay our respects on our way to Pidgeon Island.It was a very sad and moving experience.All those young men so far from their homes and families.Mostly the same age as our own kids.Beautiful sunny place,the cemetary keeper.Mr.Vasautharaja is doing a very good job of maintaining the lovely gardens and each grave has a flowering shrub.He showed his collection of photos some from his father's time as grave keeper .We saw the list of their parents names and addresses,even their middle names,we thought of those parents and their awful loss.
title: Very moving experience

body: Our driver stopped here on the way to Trincomalee which we were visiting in order to find an ATM. It was unexpected but well worth a visit. A well looked after cemetery, we met one of the gardeners. Every grave had a different flowering shrub. So many young sailors are buried here, many only 18.
title: Beautifully kept war graves, so poignant to visit, so many young lives lost.

body: Very easy to find on the main road in Uppuweli. This is beautifully maintained by the onsite caretaker who also provided us with a wealth of knowledge. Highly recommend a visit.
title: Beautifully maintained War Cemetery

body: This was a well manicured cemetery that had the graves of world war ii commonwealth soldiers who died in Sri Lanka.
title: Resting spot

body: This is one of the well maintain cemeteries that I have seen . the landscaping tells everything about itA place that holds important part of history in sri lanka
title: Saw it on the way..

body: Interesting to walk around, very clean and well kept.There are many gravestones for Air/Navel and Army personnel from all over the commonwealth.
title: Very well Kept.

body: Like all of the war cemetery's we visited in Sri Lanka it is well tended clean and tidy and thankfully does not have to many graves.
title: Very tidy cemetery

body: What ever your faith or belief it is well worth walking around this place it is so well kept & so sad to see so many young lives wasted.
title: well kept

body: This small well maintained cemetery on the main road north out of Trincomalee provides a reminder of times past when the World was a war
title: Always worth a visit

body: Very peaceful place. Very well taken care of. Stopped by here on the way back from a trip. Walked around and showed respect to those who gave the ultimate sacrifice.
title: Beautful

body: This is beautifully kept. The caretaker is very knowledgeable and will show people round, answering any questions.
title: A beautiful peaceful place

body: I couldn't go inside, but very keen to go and have a look of the peaceful RIP place, may visit soon after get to know the procedure. i was able to view and observe from out side only. Recommend tourist to vist this memorial place.
title: Peaceful RIP

body: The caretaker of this peaceful cemetery is devoted to keeping it perfect and has a great knowledge of all those remembered here. He is keen to escort you round and tell you about each grave. It was close to our hotel and we were pleased to have found it by chance.
title: Beautifully tended

body: We passed this lovely cemetery on our way to Trincomalee airport and, although there was no time to stop, we could see that it was beautifully looked after. Our driver told us that there were German as well as British and Allied military buried there, and we were very pleased to hear that.
title: We didn't actually stop but.......

body: We paused for a few minutes on our busy tour of Sri Lanka when we found ourselves by the Trincomalee War Graves. The peaceful setting and beautifully kept grounds provided a moment of quiet reflection. Each grave tells a small story - a young man (mostly) whose life was brought to an early end on a during or soon after the second world war. I counted men more than twenty ships names, and all the British armed services were represented. The war dead of other nations are also buried here. t's a beautiful place I'm glad we went.
title: Very moving and beautiful memorial

body: Very well kept war cemetery. Humbling to see how many people from a wide age group (as young as in their late teens / early twenties), representing so many nationalities have died for our freedom.
title: Humbling

body: So many Tamils laid to rest here after civil war in country. Sad to see so many graves of children.i felt quite saddened by it all !!
title: Tragedy !!

body: Peaceful and well kept oasis on the road between Upaveli and Nilaveli. Apparently the caretaker is very knowledgable, but the workers sitting around when I visited were not particularly helpful.
title: Moving commemoration of fallen soldiers

body: One of Trinco's great attractions, with great historical and cultural value. This place is immaculate and a pleasure to the eye. The lawns are manicured daily and the vicinity is properly maintained throughout the year.Highly recommended tourist attraction!
title: A Must visit in Trinco

body: We stopped in front of this War Cemetery - surrounded by a low wall and gated. It looks like it is from another world when you are in this part of Sri Lanka. Exceptionally well maintained but totally disconnected from the true Sri Lanka
title: Beautifully maintained war cemetry

body: The British war cemetery in Trincomalee has tombs of British army,navy and airforce officers who died in Sri Lanka between 1939 and 1945 (The year the country won freedom from the British) It's a heart opening place where you see so many young officers had given life for a pointless war and buried in a country so far away from their homeland.
title: A place to visit

body: This is the best kept cemetery in Sri Lanka, was very moving . The men who tough for the world were very young. So sad yet proud
title: Beautiful

body: It is beautifully maintained, and the curator has all sorts of interesting information to hand out to visitors.
title: Very interesting

body: Maintained immaculately by what appears to be a local and British Trust , this is a poignant reminder of how much suffering and sadness has been seen by this region from war and conflict in it's recent history.A must visit. Also check out the graves of the Indian labourer and Pakistani war veterans alongside their English and other multinational victims of WW 2 all maintained by a local keeper.
title: Fitting monument to the recent history of this beautiful port

body: A beautifully maintained British War Cemetery which is an unusual sight in Sri Lanka going by the other ordinary cemeteries found in the country . It stands as a permanent monument to remind us of all the British Soldiers who laid down their lives whilst based in Ceylon as it was then known during World War2.
title: A virtual Oasis in the desert

body: Such a beautiful, sad, and respectful place which is immaculately kept by the Sri Lankans. Well worth a visit to pay your respects to the fallen of WW2 who lost their lives around the Indian Ocean.
title: Beautifully maintained and very sad

body: Beautifully and respectfully tended, it is an oasis of silence and spirituality. Due to some dramatic bombardment, doctors, nurses, civilians and soldiers, many of them in their early twenties, passed away in this region in the very last days of WWII. Christians, Muslims, Hindus and Buddhists are resting side by side. Epigraphs written by parents or young spouses pay honor to the loved ones sacrificed to the absurdity of war, moving words trying to make sense of something that cannot have sense. God bless all of them.
title: a must see to think of the absurdity of wars and to celebrate humanity

body: It is near the tricomali also known as Trinco fort.no one was there to explain us .Hence no more information .
title: Just watched it

body: I think you'd need a lot of time to want to tour this site, but we did stop the car and took a photo as we passed by. It is a pretty place
title: pretty place we saw from the car window

body: This cemetery was unknown to our driver and he was grateful that we had decided to stop here. We had not realised how heavily this area of Sri Lanka had suffered in the WW2 and walked around the well kept cemetery with the caretaker who had taken on the job from his father and who will pass the job on to his son. The caretaker was very proud to show us old pictures of his family with royalty.Entrance is free but expect to reward the caretaker with a tip!
title: Delightful hillside war cemetary

body: This War Heros Cemetry was within walking distance from the Chaaya Blu hotel .It is immaculately kept and was from 1939 to 1945 war.Very moving ,reminded me of the war cemeteries in France.
title: Quite Moving

body: This is a well maintained place related to WW2. The story behind this place is sad. We should protect his place.
title: Great to see a Historical Place

body: We felt it only right whilst in the area to pay a short visit to the commonwealth war cemetery. Wonderfully kept place and a very moving spot in Trinco. Very peaceful and humbling. A must visit to pay my respect to the fallen.
title: Important to remember

body: We were surprised to see this as the number 1 thing to do and it was only a short walk from our hotel. The cemetery is small but well maintained and you should visit if you are staying nearby or driving past.At the going down of the sun,And in the morning, We will remember them.
title: Touching and well kept

body: Stopped as a extra stop. Overseas war casultes buried here from nz , au and us. Found the grounds keeper who was rd generation looking after the cemetary. He was very knowlegable and shoed us the 4 graves of the nzed. Very moving
title: Very moving place

body: As the title says it is a relatively modest but very well maintained cemetery. Right on the main road heading north out of Trincomalee, easy walking distance from the main cluster of tourist resorts. We spend 20 minutes there and that was enough to look over each headstone - my father was based in Trincomalee during WWII so he had a few old colleagues buried there
title: Modest but very well kept

body: Beautifully kept as are all of the War Graves. On a busy road but so peaceful. Well worth stopping for a few moments.
title: Sad and peaceful.

body: The cemetery is a very fitting tribute to the fallen. It is well maintained and cared for by the staff.
title: A fitting tribute to the fallen

body: Very well kept cemetery with several hundred Graves. A lot of them are from after the conclusion of the 2nd world war. Worth a visit if passing.
title: Well maintained

body: We visited this WW2 war cemetery and were impressed by the care and attention lavished on the gravestones and surrounding garden. Sobering to read the names and ages on the stones from all over the Commonwealth who gave their all for our future. A credit to the custodian and his parents before him for such a tranquil place.
title: Quiet oasis

body: Had a glance. Was built between 1959-1945. Love how they still keep it. Emphasizes the colonial era in Sri Lankan history. its on the way to Nilaweli. Don't forget to stop & have a look.
title: Peace of mind

body: This is a British military cemetery in Trincomalee, Sri Lanka, for soldiers of the British Empire who were killed or died during World War II. The cemetery is located on the Trincomalee–Nilaveli Road. It is one of the six Commonwealth war cemeteries in Sri Lanka, and maintained by Sri Lankan Ministry of Defense on behalf of the Commonwealth War Graves Commission.
title: a must visit!

body: Very well maintained. Worth visiting, but there is also one in Kandy which is very similar. You can get coconut drink outside... they add sugar and lime to it.
title: Very well kept

body: Maintain by the Navy. You can see how the Trinco fort was built in ancient SL. Also about the boats ships and the harbor. How our forces destroy LTTE boats. Great for young once and the students. Nominal fee has to be paid.
title: Great place to visit

body: Visited for a short while on the way Nilaveli. Nicely kept and peacefull. Do not read the grave stones unless you want to break your heart thinking how young they were..
title: Peacefull and Clean

body: A beautiful spot in the hustle and bussel of the area, we were welcomed and given a tour and history lesson a must if you are in the area
title: Beautifully kept

body: This is an interesting place for British travelers.On the way to Nilaveli it is worth a brake for 20 minutes to honor all these young people who died for their country.Very well maintained.
title: Very well kept ww 2 cemetry.

body: A well maintained peaceful and lovely cemetery. Worth a visit. Interestingly, the gravestones are separated into sections - Christian, Hindu, Muslim and one lonely little stone for an unknown Burmese soldier.
title: Lovely peaceful cemetery

body: Beautifully maintained and very calm and peaceful. A real credit to the caretaker who showed us around and then told us that his father had done this job before and that his son would take over from him.
title: War Cemetery

body: It is an important place to see in Trincomalee that many locals are not aware of. It's well maintained and a peaceful cemetery on the main road to Nilaveli from Trinco town.
title: An important place to see

body: Excellently kept by the Custodian. He is a wealth of knowledge and will be pleased to give you some of the background to the cemetery.
title: Well worth the visit

body: Beautifully kept. Current caretaker is son of former caretaker. Family tradition and commitment. Within easy walking distance of the Chaaya Blu. They were all so young - 364 brave souls gave their today for our tomorrow.
title: Makes you think and reflect

body: The cemetery is beautifully maintained and the custodian has a detailed knowledge of the background of all those are buried there. It was touching to see that in death, all were equal and that graves were not arranged according to rank, race or religion.
title: A beautiful and peaceful last resting place

body: Our brief visit to Trincomalee War Cemetery was very well impressed with the level the cemetery was kept all these years. Viewing the soldiers and the years associated to their history according to the head stones was amazed the very young age they were. The peacefulness of the place had most of us spent longer time than we intended. The cemetery keeper was very attentive to his duty and took great pride in maintaining the ground.
title: Very Well Kept Cemetery

body: We have visited many commonwealth war cemeteries. Without doubt the standard of maintenance here is the finest we have seen and it does the present and past caretakers great credit. The flower and shrub displays were beautiful.
title: A very moving visit

body: This was a very well maintained War Cemetery. Although located alongside the main road it was a very peaceful place.
title: Very peaceful

body: The Trincomalee War Cemetery is the second Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery I have visited. The other was in Berlin, where I visited my uncle's grave. The Trincomalee War Cemetery is lovingly tended and we met the caretaker who came out and chatted to us and showed us around. He has a great knowledge of the graves and took the job over from his father when he retired. It is good to know that our war heroes are treated with such respect and kindness even though their remains are far from home.The quotes on the headstones from family are particularly poignant. I recommend a visit, if only to bring home the futility of war.
title: Very touching memorial

body: This is a small war cemetery on the road to Nilaveli Beach it is immaculately maintained the green lawns kept trim by the small team of gardeners and all the headstones are in very good condition a War cemetery kept respectfully by the locals; worth a visit on your way to the nearby temple or beach.
title: Well maintained respectful setting.

body: The above are the feelings experienced when visiting any of the fine gardens of remembrance maintained by the commonwealth war graves commission, Trincomalee is no exception, albeit smaller than many this does not diminish the stature of those who gave their all and for whom this is their resting place,the garden is well maintained and the attendants are only too willing to share their pride and documentation of the gardens history.It is only fitting that we are able to remember in respectful surroundings
title: peace and humility

body: Palto had once said " Only the dead see the end of a war " , Probably the uniform serenity in the manner the tombstones are laid, adds the chill to the valour of those laid to rest. Probably a reminder that mother earth is one home backyard to us all . Death during a war , seems like a visa to be buried in the soil of another country and also the result of the war mongers of yesteryear who sat on the realms of power and make wrong decisions, that took the lives of many. - Remember the song "Where have all the Flowers Gone", and then remember the part " When will they ever learn " It still valid for today.
title: Well Kept Memorial

body: A poignant memorial to those young soldiers who fell to the enemy during WWII. Reading a few tombstones one is saddened that some kids hardly 18 years old who had joined the forces, are buried thousands of miles away from their homelands.
title: May they rest in peace!

body: Worth visiting this place. Well maintained. Military service personnel who sacrificed their lives are resting here.
title: Worth a visit !

body: This is a well kept reminder of the tragedy when war ships were bombed during the 2nd World war well kept by a Sri Lankan family.
title: A well kept reminder

body: Worth a visit to this place and pay our respect to the once who have sacrificed their lives during World War
title: Very well maintained place.

body: Immaculate condition and looked after by the same family since 1945. They give you an article to read which tells about the role of Ceylon during World War 2
title: Trin War cemetery

body: The cemetery is very well maintained and the guardian is very proud to show you around. His father was the guardian of the cemetery and they have very nice picture of Princess Ann, visiting the place in 1992.
title: Worth a visit

body: Nothing much to see unless you´re interested in World War II and know the history. Please take a historical guide with you.
title: Tombstones and a Tree

body: Beautiful and moving place. Well kept and worth a visit, good groundsman who explained lots to us. Not a big place so good for a quick visit
title: Beautiful and moving place.

body: Gem of a place located on Nilaveli Road . Not too difficult to find . No entrance fee. Well maintained . Serene place for those departed souls. Was lucky enough to meet the head Gardner who gave us a chapter out of our history book . Simply remarkable attention to detail . A must visit for anyone who comes to Trinco
title: Virtual History Lesson

body: As expected a well kept cemetery. We were welcomed by the caretaker who takes great pride in his work and wanted to make sure everybody understood the history behind this cemetery.Some of the headstones show damage from the recent civil unrest whilst others have been recently replaced. A moving reminder to previous conflicts and well worth visiting for a few minutes to remember those who died in a distant land.
title: Very friendly and helpful head gardener

body: lovely person and very helpful that showed us round, well kept , they have a visitors book to sign and you can spend as long or as little time that you would like to there.
title: well kept

body: Small, very clean and well maintained, in a pretty green hill, this cemetery is like a jump in the past!
title: a little jem

body: The gentleman who cared for this cemetery was a proud man who showed us photographs of when his father was in charge and Princess Ann visited and planted a tree. The cemetery is beautifully kept and there are some very interesting graves to see. The tree Princess Ann planted is quite large now.
title: Never Forget

body: A nice cemetery to have a walk around. People are there to give you more information about the cemetery if you want it, we said no and they didn't keep pushing the fact.
title: peaceful

body: Credit to the Commonwealth War Graves Commission. A tranquil and fitting memorial to those young men who rest here.
title: Peaceful resting place

body: This Second World War cemetery is relatively small in comparison to the other in Asia. However it is very well maintained and give a serene atmosphere throughout. Our group which composed of some British and Australian spent quite sometime in the cemetery observing the name, age, and year on the head stones. We were curious that some of the dates on the head stones were actually after end of the war. No one was able to explain to us on this mystery.
title: Well Maintained Cemetery

body: This Commonwealth cemetery does not cover a large area, so we can be thankful the losses while still sad for all, were not great in numbers, around 600 killed during world war 2. It has the same aura as any well maintained war cemetery and gravestones are cause for reflection, thanks and respect.
title: beautifully maintained

body: This small but beautifully maintained cemetery has so many different cultures and types of headstones. I visited cause my brother and father are huge history buffs and I was shown 4 Canadian grave sites. I will now get them to find out mor about Sri Lanka's role in WWII.
title: Interesting historical find

body: I visited because a great uncle is buried there , but a great historic site to see , beautifully maintained and beautiful to see , interesting to read some of the headstones , tells a real story .
title: well kept

body: Trincomalee War Cemetery is another beautiful example of a well kept memorial to the men and women who died during the Second World War. The site is close to the main road but as soon as you enter the grounds you are surrounded by calm. An essential opportunity to stop and reflect....
title: Peace and reflection

body: It is quite a peaceful place. The gardens are nicely maintained. The sunset from there was worth a capture.
title: Can be considered for a quick visit

body: This was a delight,so beautifully kept and tended. the gentleman showing us around was very gentle and Respectful, showing us photos of his Father in situ when HRH the Princess Anne visited and planted a tree ,he showed great pride in his work and told us that HIs son was being trained to take the reigns when he retired a wonderful memory thank you.
title: Serenity

body: Fully worth the time spent if you're already in Trinco. Very pleasant location and maintained in perfect condition.
title: Different to the normal cemetery you would expect to see

body: This was our 2nd visit to this Cemetery and like all the war cemeteries we have visited is kept in beautiful condition it's so peaceful. The person who looks after it takes his responsibility with great pride, having met his father before I can understand how important this job is to him. He is very knowledgeable and helpful even telling a group of locals to be quiet and more respectful. Those young men and women of many nationalities gave their lives for us and we should be so grateful to them for the freedom we have today.
title: We thank them for our freedom

body: The guy who looked after it was so nice ,i took flowers and laid them on the cross ,it was kept immaculate ,very peaceful .
title: well kept

body: Was on a group tour. When offered the opportunity to stop and look, 6 of us grabbed the chance and got off the bus, and went over. Welcomed by the keeper who is extremely knowledgeable of who is there. He took over after his father retired. They being the only two who have maintained these grounds beautifully. He told us that there were 303 graves of which 5 are New Zealanders. He could lead us directly to them. It is a peaceful calm place and we are grateful that we were able to photograph the headstones. We plan to make these available on the web for all.
title: We found out that there are 5 NZers there.

body: Beautifully kept, small commonwealth war cemetery. The young age of the men who sacrificed their life's is heartbreaking. As a commonwealth cemetery many nationalities are remembered here, but mainly British Royal and Merchant mariners.
title: Moving experience

body: this modern cemetary is full of caracter. Very well maintained, we were very friendly welcomed and could make pictures everywhere we wanted, in a respectful way. Good place for reflections about the very hard time people had to survive, especially in this area. It was a surprise to discover such a peaceful place outsite Trinco. Worth visiting.
title: peaceful place

body: It is a beautiful cemetery. In fact, it is THE prettiest I have seen in Sri Lanka. We looked at it while being in the vehicle right outside the cemetery and since it was quite hot at that time, we did not go in. So I can't say much.
title: Calm place

body: The 1939-1945 War Cemetry not only honours the fallen, but is a tribute to the custodians who maintain and care for it. It's set a bit out of town, but that only adds to the surroundings. All the graves are beautifully maintained, with bright coloured plants to add just that bit of brightness. The custodians must also be credited with holding an extensive range of records relating both the fallen who are buried here and the bombing of Trincomalee.We would rate this Commonwealth War Cemetry with a 10/10 to match Kandy (Sri Lanka) and Adelaide River (Northern Territory, Australia)
title: A Fitting Tribute

body: Having stayed on Sober island I felt my visit to Trinco would be incomplete if I did not visit the Trinco War cemetery. It was a well kept place and interesting to wander around reading the epitahs and names of those who had laid down their lives .
title: A different tourist excursion

body: went here whilst holidaying in trinco in august so beautifully kept peaceful tranquil it was a scorching day but the watering system was in place The guy who looks after it told us that the British government helps to pay for its upkeep what a n appropriate place to remember all the lives which were lost
title: a peaceful place

body: The headstones of the fallen of WW2 from many countries are set in this immaculately kept cemetery. A tribute to the gardeners who keep it in such beautiful condition.
title: A beautiful place

body: This cemetery is very well maintained. It is a very interesting place, but has a conflicting history.
title: Worth seeing

body: This is not a large war cemetery but it is full of history and is the resting place of many servicemen from around the world. The grounds keeper does an amazing job of keeping this place in such beautiful condition. He takes pride in his work and shows the servicemen the respect they are due. Worth a look.
title: A place to reflect

body: A visit to the Commonwealth Cemetery is a must do when visiting Trinco. It is not only Australian, New Zealanders and Brits laid to rest in this green and perfectly kept oasis. The Dutch, French, Indian and a few other warriors and nurses are laid to rest in the tribute to the fallen.It's about fifteen minutes drive form the city, on the way to Nilaveli. The guardian is second generation of this family to preserve this war memorial, and will inform and guide with respect to any graves you are interested in. I found a visit here very moving, not only for the tragic loss, but for the care that this cemetery is watched over.
title: Humbling, A must visit.

body: A lovely quiet oasis in a mad world to reflect on the lives lost . The cemetery is so well looked after.
title: Beautiful place

body: This cemetery is a credit to the man who maintains it. His father had that task before him and such is his dedication that he knows the name of every person interred there and the location of each grave. Most of the soldiers were killed by bombing of ships in the Trincomalee harbour which is the fifth largest natural harbour in the world. There were even two Australians buried there. It was a moving experience to visit and stroll through the cemetery.
title: Immaculately maintained

body: Well worth a visit if local history is of interest. The cemetary is very well maintained. and not too far to travel too. If interested in details allow a bit of time to browse through the cemetary.
title: part of local history

body: It was very hot and sunny, with no shade, but we spent quite a long time here. Like all Commonwealth War Graves Commission Cemeteries, it was beautifully maintained, and like several graveyards we visited in Sri Lanka, it had been maintained by one family for many years. It was moving to see (mainly) Naval personnel from all over the Commonwealth and of all ranks and religions given equally beautiful headstones. The Custodian was rightly proud of it, and we were glad we gave up the time to remember those who were largely bombed in ships in the harbour and in shore establishments in Sri Lanka. (We had to look up the various ships, despite being keen Naval history buffs - it was a part of the war not much written about).
title: Beautifully maintained memorial

body: Beautifully kept tribute to those who gave the ultimate sacrifice. Needs a dedicated parking area to attract more visitors - very hard to safely pull off the road.
title: Well-kept Memorial

body: This Commonwealth War Graves Commission site is know locally as the 'British Cemetery'. Two to three hundred rupee tuk tuk ride from town, or a 900 local bus. You are met by a second generation curator who will escort you In this beautiful spot there are 362 graves of which two are Australian, 328 British, and a whole mixture of other fairs and nationalities, even the Indian labourers, mostly with only one anglicised name, are even remembered here. It was set up in 1947' and even has graves for people who dies aft the 39-45 war. During the civil war there was an engagement between the SLArmy helicopters and the LTTE (Tamil tigers) which damaged 22 of the headstones, the ones that were not replaced the damage can still be seen. (Eg. Scrivener) Some graves had the usual religions and like epitaph engraved but I loved wasa serjeant(sic) G.A.Kyle whose epitaph was 'curry anything'.
title: Beautiful sanctuary for the living as well as the dead

body: Amazing to see the graves so well maintained after all these years. In absolute pristine condition. Definitely worth a visit. The chap running the show is part of a family who have looked after the site since the world war - nice guy.
title: Pristine condition

body: everything is like what it was many years ago now it is really excellent specially after the 30 year war
title: well maintained like British standards not sls
Very Moving Cemetery well tended
body: This oasis of green and calm on the edge of Trinco is just so very moving. The headstones chart the loss of life of mainly naval personnel and airmen who came under tremendous attack during the war and some died well after the war was won and are buried here too. The Gardener will take you around and give you some information to read, and some of the headstones have been bullet holed in the latest Civil war so they are being replaced. The Jewish, Moslem and Christian faiths are represented and Kiwis, Aussies, Brits, Dutch, Malay, Indian and Sri Lankans are all buried together

title: Beautifully maintained
body: Peaceful, respectful place. Such young men dying makes one weep. It was a moving tribute to soldiers everywhere.

title: Not sure if this place gets the recognition it is due.
body: Whilst one of the best maintained war cemetaries in Sri Lanka, I am not sure if the existence of the Trincomalee war cemetary is known to many. It certainly is not listed in any of the tourist maps as a place to visit. And fully worth a visit it is, especially if you are a war historian or someone who's family or country has been touched by the second world war. This is primarily a British war cemetary and maintained (beautifully I must say) from a grant from England. You are not allowed to film or take photos here, but just a stroll amongst the tombstones of the fallen, is a very poignant and sobering experience.

title: A beautiful place to reflect!
body: The WWII cemetery is beautifully kept and serves as a fitting memorial to those who lost their lives in the Second World War. The guardian is extremely helpful and treats the place as though it was his own. He took over the job from his father. Most of the British dead were in the Navy and with them lie friends from India, Canada and Sri Lanka.
